ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare-review request with no refund; keep the trip record as-is (no RD-1 breach recorded, since the single off-route segment is RD-5-exempt).

segment_findings.reason: RD-5 exemption: the driver proposed the route change before leaving the optimal route (F7, 10:01, naming 'go round via Halus Link') and the rider expressly agreed (F8, 10:01, 'Sure, go ahead'), both timestamps preceding the segment start of 10:04 (F3). Consent covers the named Halus Link corridor, and the executed segment goes where the driver said it would (1.94 km / +1.73 km on that corridor), not somewhere other than what was named; the agreement contains no limitation to part of the excursion. RD-3/RD-4 add nothing: no rider-requested stop (RD-3) and no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, only band 4 corroboration (F10, F11, F12; RD-4(b)). [F3][F7][F8][F10][F11][F12][RD-5][RD-4]

rejected_claims.reason: The 1.8 km / +18% figure (F1) does not by itself establish an unexempted deviation: RD-1's shortest-route duty is qualified by 'absence of reasonable cause', and here the single deviation was pre-approved by the rider (F7, F8) before it began at 10:04 (F3), which is the RD-5 exemption [F1][F3][F7][F8][RD-1][RD-5].

The segment's size (F3: 1.94 km vs 0.22 km optimal, +1.73 km, up to 947 m off route) is accepted and is not treated as map-matching noise, but magnitude does not defeat the RD-5 exemption once the rider agreed to that named route before departure [F3][F7][F8][RD-1][RD-5].

Correct on the traffic record (no incidents near the route [F12]; speed band 4 on Tampines Expressway and Punggol Road [F10][F11], which RD-4(b) treats as corroboration at best) — but RD-4 only decides segments lacking consent; the driver does not need a traffic justification for the route he named and the rider approved [F10][F11][F12][F7][F8][RD-4][RD-5].

Rejected: RD-5 consent is not confined to the stated reason for the reroute. The driver named the route ('go round via Halus Link' [F7]) and the rider gave an unconditional agreement [F8]; the scope rule exempts the segment unless it plainly goes somewhere other than what was named, and the executed segment runs on that named corridor [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. Rebuttal's 'must be scoped to the Tampines Expressway build-up' reading imports a limit that appears nowhere in F7 or F8 [F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

Conceded and confirmed: as a non-metered RydeX fixed-quote trip, the billed distance was 9.9 km equal to the optimal route with surge 1.0× [F4][F5], so the deviation produced no recoverable mileage undercharge, and no unpublished add-on exists [F6][RD-2][FARE-1].
Conceded and confirmed: the itemisation $3.90 + $14.02 + $3.93 + $1.47 = $23.32 with waiting $0.00 and no ERP/toll or manual line item leaves nothing refundable under FARE-1 [F6][FARE-1].

Rejected: RD-6's precondition is a case established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach), and neither exists here — the lone segment is RD-5-exempt and the refund computes to $0; F15 also shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, and profile facts cannot decide the case [F3][F15][RD-6].

Partially rejected: the band 4 reading (30–39 km/h, F10) is not a reasonable cause under RD-4(b) and cannot excuse the segment on its own; the driver's exemption rests on RD-5 consent, not on traffic [F10][F12][RD-4][RD-5].

Rejected to the extent it seeks a flag on the basis of dispute count: RD-6 requires an established breach first, which fails here (exempt segment, $0 refund); F15's 0 upheld route disputes and 321 trips would in any case not establish 'repeated' [F3][F15][RD-6].
